# User Stories — Dragon R1 (from PRD)

*Generated by story-generator agent from PRD-Dragon-R1.md. Use for sprint planning and acceptance testing.*

---

# User Story 1: إنشاء مشروع | Create Project

**As a** penetration tester or engagement manager  
**I want** to create a new project with a name, scope, and settings  
**So that** I can group all tasks, tests, and reports under one client or campaign.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I am logged in and on the projects page  
**When** I choose to create a new project and enter a name and scope (e.g. web only, web + network)  
**Then** the system creates the project, stores it (and optional settings), and I see it in my project list and can open it.

**Given** a new project exists  
**When** I open it  
**Then** I see its details, linked tasks, and any associated reports.

---

# User Story 2: إنشاء مهمة مرتبطة بمشروع | Create Task Linked to Project

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** to create a task and link it to a project  
**So that** every execution (recon, exploitation, report) is tied to that engagement.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I am on the "Create task" flow (e.g. from `/tasks/new` or from a project)  
**When** I enter the target (IP, URL, or scope) and select a project from the list  
**Then** the system creates the task, links it to the chosen project, and shows confirmation (e.g. via WebSocket or API).

**Given** a task was created with a project  
**When** I view the project  
**Then** that task appears in the project's task list.

---

# User Story 3: عرض المهام حسب المشروع | View Tasks per Project

**As a** penetration tester or manager  
**I want** to see all tasks belonging to a project in one place  
**So that** I can track progress and results per engagement.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a project has one or more tasks  
**When** I open the project (e.g. `/projects` → select project)  
**Then** I see a list of all tasks for that project with status and key info.

**Given** I am viewing a project's tasks  
**When** I click a task  
**Then** I am taken to the task detail view (e.g. `/tasks/[id]`) with execution progress and results.

---

# User Story 4: تنفيذ المرحلة الاستطلاعية فقط | Informational Phase Execution (Recon Only)

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** the system to run only reconnaissance (no exploitation) by default  
**So that** I get discovery results without any high-risk actions until I approve them.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a task is in the Informational phase  
**When** the agent runs  
**Then** only recon and discovery actions run (e.g. 6-phase recon); no exploitation or post-exploitation is executed.

**Given** recon has produced results  
**When** I view the task or graph  
**Then** findings (domains, IPs, ports, services, potential vulns) are visible and stored (e.g. Neo4j, mem0) without any exploitation having been run.

---

# User Story 5: طلب موافقة قبل الاستغلال | Approval Request Before Exploitation

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** to be asked for explicit approval before the system runs exploitation  
**So that** I control when high-risk actions occur.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** the agent has found potential vulnerabilities and wants to move to Exploitation  
**When** it requests phase transition  
**Then** an approval dialog appears showing the planned action and justification.

**Given** the approval dialog is open  
**When** I choose [Approve], [Reject], or [Request more info]  
**Then** the system records my choice and proceeds only if I approved; rejection prevents exploitation.

---

# User Story 6: فترة تبريد قبل تنفيذ الإجراء المعتمد | Cooling Period Before Approved Action

**As a** security-conscious user  
**I want** a mandatory cooling period (e.g. 300 seconds) after I approve a high-risk action  
**So that** I have a last chance to cancel or reconsider.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I have approved an exploitation or post-exploitation action  
**When** the system accepts the approval  
**Then** it waits for the configured cooling period (e.g. 300 s) before executing the action.

**Given** the cooling period is active  
**When** I cancel or revoke the approval (if supported)  
**Then** the high-risk action is not executed.

---

# User Story 7: الموافقة صراحةً لمرحلة ما بعد الاستغلال | Explicit Approval for Post-Exploitation

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** separate explicit approval before post-exploitation (e.g. privilege escalation, lateral movement)  
**So that** escalation actions are never automatic.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** exploitation has succeeded and the agent wants to run post-exploitation  
**When** it requests transition to Post-exploitation  
**Then** an approval workflow is shown (same pattern as for Exploitation) with clear description of the planned actions.

**Given** I have not approved post-exploitation  
**When** the agent would run post-exploitation  
**Then** those actions are not executed; approval workflows cannot be bypassed.

---

# User Story 8: تنفيذ أدوات MCP الخمس عشرة | Execute 15 MCP Tools

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** the system to run the 15 MCP tools (e.g. kali_shell, nmap, nuclei, naabu, hydra, sqlmap, metasploit, curl, code execution, web_search, query_graph, reverse_engineering, malware_analysis, forensics)  
**So that** recon, exploitation, and analysis are done with the right tools.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** the agent needs to scan ports or run a security tool  
**When** it selects an MCP tool (e.g. execute_nmap, execute_nuclei, kali_shell)  
**Then** the Gateway runs the tool with validation, timeout, and output capture and returns results to the agent.

**Given** a tool has run  
**When** results are available  
**Then** they are parsed, stored in Neo4j/mem0 where specified, and audit-logged; errors trigger retry or alternative tool where applicable.

---

# User Story 9: خط أنابيب الاستطلاع ذو الست مراحل | Six-Phase Recon Pipeline

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** recon to run in six ordered phases (domain discovery → port scan → HTTP probing → resource enumeration → vulnerability scanning → MITRE enrichment)  
**So that** discovery is systematic and feeds the graph and memory.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a task is in the Informational phase and recon is started  
**When** the pipeline runs  
**Then** phases run in order: (1) domain discovery (e.g. crt.sh, Amass, WHOIS, DNS), (2) port scanning (e.g. Naabu, Nmap), (3) HTTP probing (e.g. httpx, Wappalyzer), (4) resource enumeration (e.g. Katana, GAU, Kiterunner), (5) vulnerability scanning (e.g. Nuclei), (6) MITRE enrichment (CWE/CAPEC/ATT&CK).

**Given** each phase completes  
**When** results are produced  
**Then** they are written to Neo4j and mem0 so the graph and agent can use them in later phases and reporting.

---

# User Story 10: توليد التقرير وعرضه | Report Generation and Display

**As a** penetration tester or client  
**I want** a comprehensive report (executive summary, findings, MITRE mapping, recommendations) after a task completes  
**So that** I can present results and remediation to stakeholders.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a task has completed (or I request a report on demand)  
**When** report generation is triggered  
**Then** the system produces a report from mem0 and the graph including target summary, recon results, vulnerabilities, exploits, and recommendations in the required structure.

**Given** a report has been generated  
**When** I open the reports area (e.g. `/reports`) or the task  
**Then** I can view the report; it is available in at least one of Markdown, PDF, or HTML and is stored under `/reports` and accessible via UI or API.

---

# User Story 11: بدء الستاك (Docker + Kali) | Start Docker and Kali Stack

**As a** operator or penetration tester  
**I want** to start the full stack (e.g. via `docker-compose up -d` or `start-docker-and-dragon.bat`)  
**So that** the web app, Gateway, Neo4j, mem0, and Kali (and other services) are running in one go.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** Docker is installed and the project's compose/scripts are available  
**When** I run the start command (e.g. `docker-compose up -d` or the project's start script)  
**Then** the defined containers (e.g. webapp, Gateway, Neo4j, mem0, Kali, GVM if configured) start on the same internal network (e.g. `dragon-r1-network`).

**Given** the stack has started  
**When** I open the web app (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and API (e.g. http://localhost:8000)  
**Then** they respond and I can log in and use the system (per documented defaults).

---

# User Story 12: تواصل البوابة مع حاوية Kali | Gateway Talks to Kali Container

**As a** system operator  
**I want** the Gateway to run pentest commands inside the Kali container (e.g. via `docker exec dragon-r1-kali`)  
**So that** MCP tools that need Kali (nmap, Metasploit, etc.) run in a consistent, isolated environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** the Kali container (`dragon-r1-kali`) and Gateway are on the same Docker network  
**When** the Gateway needs to run a command (e.g. for kali_shell or an MCP tool)  
**Then** it executes the command inside the Kali container with timeout and output capture; input is validated/sanitized to reduce command-injection risk.

**Given** a tool that requires Kali (e.g. Metasploit, Nmap, Hydra, Sqlmap) is invoked  
**When** the Gateway processes the request  
**Then** the payload runs inside the Kali container (or on a Kali host in Option A); results are returned to the Gateway and then to the agent/Neo4j/mem0 as designed.

---

# User Story 13: عرض التقدم والرسم البياني للمهمة | View Task Progress and Graph

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** to see live task progress and an attack-surface graph (Neo4j) for a task  
**So that** I can monitor execution and understand discovered assets and relationships.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a task is running  
**When** I open the task page (e.g. `/tasks/[id]`) or graph view (`/graph`)  
**Then** I see current phase and progress (e.g. via WebSocket updates) and a graph of nodes and relationships (e.g. Domain, IP, Port, Service, Vulnerability) for that task/project.

**Given** recon or exploitation has added data to the graph  
**When** I view the graph  
**Then** new nodes and relationships appear (with acceptable delay); I can use the graph to navigate and understand the attack surface.

---

# User Story 14: تقارير متعددة الصيغ ووصول آمن | Multiple Report Formats and Secure Access

**As a** client or engagement manager  
**I want** reports in Markdown, PDF, and HTML and access only for authorized users  
**So that** I can share the right format and control who sees sensitive findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a report has been generated for a task  
**When** I request download or view  
**Then** I can get the report in at least one of Markdown, PDF, or HTML as configured/supported.

**Given** I am not authorized to see a project or report  
**When** I try to open it (via UI or API)  
**Then** access is denied; security-relevant access attempts are audited.

---

# User Story 15: واجهة واحدة لجميع العمليات | Single Unified Web Interface

**As a** penetration tester  
**I want** one web application for dashboard, projects, tasks, graph, chat, tools, reports, and settings  
**So that** I don't switch between multiple UIs for daily work.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Given** I am using Dragon R1  
**When** I navigate the app  
**Then** I can reach dashboard, projects, tasks (list/new/detail), graph, chat, tools, reports, and settings from a single Next.js app (e.g. `/`, `/projects`, `/tasks`, `/tasks/new`, `/tasks/[id]`, `/graph`, `/chat`, `/tools`, `/reports`, `/settings`).

**Given** I perform an action that requires the backend  
**When** the app calls the API or WebSocket  
**Then** it uses the configured Gateway (e.g. JWT, REST, WebSocket) so that all features work through one interface and one backend entry point.

---

## Technical Problems Solved (Summary)

- **Project/task model:** Clear project–task linkage and scoping for engagements.  
- **Safety and control:** Three-phase model with mandatory approvals and cooling period to prevent unauthorized exploitation/post-exploitation.  
- **Tooling and recon:** 15 MCP tools and a defined 6-phase recon pipeline with consistent execution and storage in Neo4j/mem0.  
- **Reporting:** Structured, multi-format reports from a single pipeline with secure access.  
- **Deployment and execution:** Docker Compose stack with Kali container and Gateway–Kali communication for a reproducible, isolated pentest environment.  
- **UX and integration:** Single web app and real-time updates (e.g. WebSocket) for progress and graph.
